The total thermal resistance per unit area is calculated by summing the convective resistances and the conductive resistances of all layers. The heat flux is then the temperature difference divided by the total resistance. The temperature at the interface between layers 4 and 5 is found by subtracting the temperature drop across the inner convective resistance and layers 1–4 from the inside air temperature.

- Inside convective resistance: \( R_{\text{conv,in}} = 1/10 = 0.1 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
- Outside convective resistance: \( R_{\text{conv,out}} = 1/17 \approx 0.0588235 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
- Layer resistances:
  - Layer 1: \( 0.28/2.3 \approx 0.121739 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 2: \( 0.04/0.04 = 1.0 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 3: \( 0.24/1.4 \approx 0.171429 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 4: \( 0.075/1.1 \approx 0.0681818 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 5: \( 0.02/0.17 \approx 0.117647 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 6: \( 0.01/0.13 \approx 0.0769231 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 7: \( 0.015/0.12 = 0.125 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)
  - Layer 8: \( 0.075/0.17 \approx 0.441176 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)

Total resistance:  
\( R_{\text{total}} \approx 2.28092 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)

Temperature difference: \( \Delta T = 20 - (-2) = 22 \, \text{K} \)

Heat flux:  
\( q = \Delta T / R_{\text{total}} \approx 22 / 2.28092 \approx 9.6452 \, \text{W/m}^2 \) → rounded to 4 significant figures: \( 9.645 \, \text{W/m}^2 \)

Resistance from inside to interface (layers 1–4 + inside convection):  
\( R_{\text{in→if}} \approx 1.46135 \, \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W} \)

Temperature drop: \( \Delta T_{\text{in→if}} = q \cdot R_{\text{in→if}} \approx 9.6452 \times 1.46135 \approx 14.095 \, \text{K} \)

Interface temperature:  
\( T_{\text{if}} = 20 - 14.095 \approx 5.905 \,^\circ\text{C} \) → rounded to 4 significant figures: \( 5.905 \,^\circ\text{C} \)

ANSWER: 9.645, 5.905
